To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new ADC architecture has been proposed that is able to achieve a high power efficiency in moderate-resolution, medium-bandwidth applications, while being insensitive to comparator thermal noise.
the proposed noise tolerant SAR ADC architecture achieves a power efficiency of 820μW/ENOB at 40MS/s, with a power consumption that increases linearly with resolution.
the use of pre-amplified latches in SAR ADCs can reduce the impact of comparator noise, thus allowing to achieve high resolution and high power efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of SAR ADCs that are able to achieve high performance in terms of resolution and power consumption.
the design of a SAR ADC with a noise-tolerant comparator.
the design and implementation of a SAR ADC that is able to overcome the limitations imposed by comparator noise.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SAR architectures are not suited for high-resolution applications.
SAR ADCs are not suitable for high-resolution applications, and the only way to achieve high resolution is to use pipelining, which would require a large number of stages and thus a large area.
the use of dynamic regenerating latches in SAR ADCs is not the best choice in order to achieve high power and area efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a noise-tolerant SAR ADC architecture that allows to reduce the effect of comparator noise by 3.2ENOBs, with respect to the state-of-the-art, and to achieve a total power consumption of 820μW at 40MS/s, in a 90nm CMOS digital process, with a resolution of 9 bits.
we propose an alternative to the conventional SAR architecture, which can achieve a higher resolution and/or a higher sampling rate than conventional SARs with the same power consumption.
we are able to demonstrate that it is possible to achieve a 9b 10MS/s SAR ADC in 90 nm CMOS with a power consumption of 820μW.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with a suitable architecture, it is possible to achieve high power-efficiency even with comparators that are not noise-tolerant.

the use of dynamic regenerators, which are the most power-efficient solution for SAR comparators, can be reconciled with noise tolerance by using a novel dynamic comparator architecture that is able to reject comparator thermal noise.

the noise tolerance of a SAR ADC can be significantly enhanced by using an analog comparator with a pre-amplifier stage, as in a flash ADC, and a digital post-amplification stage to determine the final conversion.
